                                       PROJECT NO. 58481


    RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                              §   PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
    LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                           §
    STANDARDS UNDER PURA 37.0561                         §           OF TEXAS


           AEP TEXAS INC.’S COMMENTS ON STAFF DISCUSSION DRAFT

       AEP Texas Inc. (AEP Texas) respectfully submits these comments in response to the Staff

Discussion Draft issued by Commission Staff regarding large load interconnection standards under

PURA § 37.0561. An executive summary is provided as the last page of this filing.

          I.       RESPONSES TO QUESTIONS IN STAFF DISCUSSION DRAFT

   1. Should the Commission define parameters for determining whether a large-load customer
      is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request? If so, how should the
      Commission define those parameters?

       Yes, however AEP Texas recognizes that there may be impediments to identification of

substantially similar interconnection requests even with established parameters. For example, the

requests may be submitted to other ISO/RTOs and the requestor may be a developer that does not

have insight into other requests submitted by their clients. The parameters for determining whether

a large-load customer is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request should include a

review of the details of the requests submitted to the applicable Distribution Service Provider with

legal authority to provide retail electric delivery service (applicable DSP) and whether any of the

requests with the applicable DSP or in areas with other applicable DSPs would cause the customer

to not pursue the request if the other is granted.

   2. Proposed subsections (c)(3), (e)(3), and (h)(3) require the disclosure of specific information
      related to a substantially similar request for interconnection and allows a large load
      customer to anonymize competitively sensitive details. Should the Commission list what
      is and is not competitively sensitive (e.g., load zone is not competitively sensitive
Docket No. 58481                                                            AEP Texas Inc.’s Comments
                                                     1
         information)? If so, what information should and should not be considered competitively
        sensitive such that the interconnecting utility and ERCOT can identify whether there is a
        duplicate request, or a request is unlikely to materialize?
        No, the Commission does not need to list categories of information considered

competitively sensitive because those categories are already known to industry stakeholders. One

of the obvious ways ERCOT can identify whether there is a duplicate request is based on the

location of the large-load customer’s interconnecting facility. The most effective way to prevent

duplication of requests is to require all the reporting requirements in Senate Bill 6 to be provided

by the customer to the interconnecting electric utility. This will reduce confusion from the

customer perspective and ensure that ERCOT receives consistent information on each

interconnection request that satisfies each of the criteria required under PURA § 37.0561.

    3. Should the Commission require a large load customer to notify the interconnecting electric
       utility and ERCOT of any change to information that is initially disclosed in response to
       this rule or only material changes to the information disclosed? If only material changes,
       how should “material change” be defined.

        AEP Texas supports a requirement that large-load customers notify the interconnecting

electric utility and ERCOT about all changes to the information that was initially disclosed. To

analyze the request and ultimately connect the customer, the utilities and ERCOT need to have the

latest information about the interconnecting facility. AEP Texas also supports a requirement that

large-load customers provide ongoing updates regarding the interconnecting facility throughout

the life span of the interconnection of the facility.

    4. Proposed subsection (k)(1) authorizes an interconnecting electric utility to refund 20% of
       a large load customer’s security after energization and ratably as the large load customer
       meets the milestones identified in the customer’s schedule for phased energization of its
       contracted load. Should the Commission standardize the rate for refund for reaching
       milestones identified in the customer’s schedule for phased energization (e.g., 20% for each
       year of operations until the full amount of security is refunded)? If so, how should the
       Commission standardize the refund.

Docket No. 58481                                                            AEP Texas Inc.’s Comments
                                                   2
        Senate Bill 6 requires that standards include uniform financial commitment requirements

and then lists the types of mechanisms that can serve to provide satisfactory proof of financial

commitment.1 One of those mechanisms is security provided on a dollar per megawatt basis as set

by the Commission.2 If security is used as the mechanism for financial commitment, the security

must be refunded in whole or in part after the security is applied to amounts owed (1) as the large-

load customer meets the customer’s load ramp milestones and sustains operations for a prescribed

period as determined by the Commission; (2) if the large-load customer withdraws its request for

all or a portion of the requested capacity; or (3) if capacity subject to a financial commitment will

be reallocated to one or more customers. There is no need for the Commission to further outline

requirements for the security refund.

   5. Are changes to the Commission’s other substantive rules necessary to align with this
      rulemaking? If so, what changes need to be made to which rules?

       AEP Texas recommends that the Commission consider development of requirements that

include a standard large-load customer interconnection study form and a standard construction

service form. Standard formats will provide consistency for customers.

       AEP Texas also requests that the Commission develop standards for the way in which funds

should be transferred among utilities for circumstances when the applicable DSP facilitates the

interconnection but is not necessarily the transmission service provider (TSP) for the specific point

of interconnection.

           II.      COMMENTS ON PROPOSED 16 TEX. ADMIN. CODE § 25.194

       Subsection (b)(3) – Definition of Discretionary services agreement

       AEP Texas requests that the proposed term “discretionary services agreement,” be changed

to “construction services agreement,” as it more closely describes the contents of the agreement.

The acronym “DSA” is already used for “delivery service agreements.” AEP Texas also requests

that the Commission revise the definition to reflect that Senate Bill 6 provides options for types of

financial commitment other than securitization.

       Discretionary Construction services agreement -- An agreement, executed and
       with financial commitment securitized by a large load customer and
       interconnecting electric utility after the interconnecting electric utility completes
       the large load interconnection study and before the interconnecting electric utility
       submits the study to ERCOT, that, at a minimum, satisfies subsection (d) of this
       section.


       Subsection (b)(5) – Interconnecting electric utility
       TSPs do not have a direct relationship with the load and should not be given the ability to

dictate the viability of an interconnection request. AEP Texas requests that the definition of

“interconnecting electric utility” be revised to reflect that the relationship is between the applicable

DSP and the load.

       Interconnecting electric utility – The electric utility, municipally owned utility, or
       electric cooperative that has is the Distribution Service Provider with legal authority
       to provide retail electric delivery service. load serving responsibility. owns and
       operates the facilities necessary to interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT
       transmission network.

       Subsection (b)(6) – Intermediate agreement
       AEP Texas requests that the requirement for intermediate agreements be removed from the

rule because it requires parties to negotiate, obtain approvals, and execute another agreement when

the same outcome can be achieved via amendment of the construction services agreement. As set

out below, AEP Texas requests that the Commission make conforming changes to subsection (h).
Docket No. 58481                                                               AEP Texas Inc.’s Comments

         Subsection (c)(7) – Study fee

        Instead of setting a minimum study fee, AEP Texas requests that the Commission set the

study fee at $114,000 for 75 MW up to 250 MW and $314,000 for equal to or greater than 250

MW. AEP Texas also requests that subpart (c)(7)(D) be revised to contemplate the circumstance

when the large-load customer would need to remit payment for the study fee to the TSP if the TSP

is not the load serving entity.

        Subsection (e) – Discretionary services agreement

        AEP Texas requests that Section (e) be revised to parallel the changes proposed for

subsection (b)(3). Specifically, the term should be changed to “Construction services agreement,”

as it more closely describes the contents of the agreement and because the acronym “DSA” already

exists for delivery service agreements. Furthermore, the language should be revised to reflect that

Senate Bill 6 contemplates other types of financial commitment in addition to securitization.

        (e)     Discretionary Construction services agreement.       Before the
                interconnecting electric utility submits the large load
                interconnection study to ERCOT, the large load customer must
                execute and financially commit to securitize a discretionary
                construction services agreement that, at a minimum, includes the
                updated disclosures and financial commitments under this
                subsection.

        Subsection (e)(2) – Site control

        Large-load customers should be required to have site control for the entire duration of the

time to reach the peak demand. AEP Texas requests that the Commission remove the time

limitations proposed in subparts (e)(2)(A) and (B).

                (A)     a legally and financially binding option to purchase or lease for the proposed
                        load location for the duration of at least 50% of the expected time to reach
                        the peak demand;

                (B)     a signed and executed lease agreement for the proposed load location for
                       the duration of at least 50% of the expected time to reach the peak demand;
                       or
       Subsection (e)(8) - Financial security on a dollar per MW basis

       Large-load customers are defined as greater than 75 MW and can include different types

of loads that have access to different levels of capital at different stages of a project. AEP Texas

requests that the Commission decrease the rate for financial security to $10,000 per MW instead

of $50,000 per MW. This helps drive one of the main concepts within Senate Bill 6, to foster

economic development for various load types.

       New Subsection (e)(9) – Financial commitment for significant equipment or services

       AEP Texas proposes a new subpart to section (e) for the construction services agreement

that parallels similar language in subsection (h) regarding financial commitments for significant

equipment or services. AEP Texas proposes the language as a permissive component at this stage

to provide customers with flexibility should they want to provide payment prior to the large-load

interconnection study (LLIS).

               Financial commitment for significant equipment or services. Before the
               interconnecting electric utility procures equipment or services, a large load
               customer may pay its required financial commitment to the interconnecting
               utility in an amount equal to the interconnecting electric utility’s expected
               costs for equipment with a lead time of at least six months and services
               necessary to interconnect the large load customer. The interconnecting
               electric utility may accept the following forms of payment for financial
               security for significant equipment or services:
               (A)      cash collateral;
               (B)      corporate or parental guaranty, only if the corporation or parent
                        corporation has a credit rating equivalent of BBB-/Baa3 or higher
                        from a recognized bond rating firm; or
               (C)      a letter of credit issued by a bank with a credit rating equivalent of
                        BBB/Baa3 or higher from a recognized bond rating firm.

        New subsection (e)(10) Contribution in aid of Construction

       AEP Texas proposes to add a second new subpart to subsection (e) for the construction

services agreement that parallels similar language proposed in subsection (h) regarding

contribution in aid of construction (CIAC). AEP Texas proposes that this language is also intended

to provide a permissive component at this stage to provide customers with flexibility should they

want to provide payment prior to the large-load interconnection study (LLIS).

               Contribution in aid of construction (CIAC). Before the interconnecting
               electric utility begins construction of facilities to interconnect a large load
               customer, a large load customer may pay CIAC in an amount that is equal
               to the interconnecting electric utility’s expected costs to interconnect the
               large load customer and that are directly attributable to interconnecting the
               large load customer.
               (A)     Costs directly attributable to interconnecting the large load customer
                       include all costs associated with one or more new transmission lines
                       built to interconnect the large load customer to the existing
                       transmission network, including substation upgrades associated
                       with interconnecting the new large load customer.
               (B)     Costs associated with system upgrades that would not be required
                       but for the interconnecting large load customer are costs directly
                       attributable to the interconnecting large load customer. Where a
                       system upgrade is necessary to serve multiple large load customers,
                       such system upgrade costs must be pro-rated among those large load
                       customers based on the contracted peak demand of each of those
                       customers.
               (C)     For a large load customer that is interconnecting to an existing
                       transmission asset, costs directly attributable to interconnecting the
                       large load customer include a share of the original CIAC that another
                       large load customer paid under this section. The share of original
                       CIAC must be calculated based on remaining net book value of the
                       associated costs as a fraction of the original book value of those
                       costs, and further pro-rated based on the share of contracted peak
                       demand of the new large load customer as a fraction of the aggregate
                       contracted peak demand of all large load customers associated with
                       that transmission asset, including the new large load customer.
                       CIAC payments under this subsection must be credited to the
                       previous large load customers that contributed to the previous CIAC
                       payments, on an asset by asset basis, in proportion to those previous
                       payments.

       Subsection (f) Submission of large load interconnection study to ERCOT

       AEP Texas requests that the word “discretionary” be replaced with “construction” to

comport with other revisions AEP Texas has proposed. Additionally, if a large-load customer fails

to execute and securitize a construction services agreement, AEP Texas requests that the period

within which an interconnecting utility must cancel the interconnection requested and notify

ERCOT of the cancellation be increased to 90 days from the proposed 30 days. The construction

services agreements will be difficult to execute within a short window of 30 days.

       Subsection (h) – Intermediate service agreement

       As noted above, AEP Texas requests that parties be permitted to amend construction

services agreements in lieu of entering into intermediate service agreements. AEP Texas requests

that the title of subsection (h) be revised to be “Construction services agreement - amendments,”

and the language in subsection (h) be revised to reflect that the agreement will be amended instead

of executed.

       Intermediate Construction services agreement - amendments. Not later than 180
       days after the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT complete the large load
       interconnection study for a large load customer, the large load customer must
       execute amend and securitize the an intermediate construction services agreement
       with the interconnecting electric utility that, at a minimum, includes the updated
       disclosures and financial commitments under this subsection. The interconnecting
       electric utility must cancel the interconnection request and notify ERCOT of the
       cancellation if the large load customer fails to pay the execute and securitizeCIAC
       and amend the construction services intermediate agreement under this subsection
       within 180 days of the interconnecting electric utility and ERCOT’s completion of
       all necessary transmission studies to interconnect the large load customer.

       AEP Texas requests that the title of subpart (h)(8) be revised so that it is “Financial

Additionally, AEP Texas requests that the first sentence of subpart (h)(8) be revised to reflect that

a large-load customer would not have to make a financial commitment if it had already done so

       the interconnecting electric utility procures equipment or services, a large load
       customer must pay make a financial security commitment, unless this payment was
       executed in the initial Construction Services Agreement, to the interconnecting
       utility in an amount equal to the interconnecting electric utility’s expected costs for
       equipment with a lead time of at least six months and services necessary to
       interconnect the large load customer.
       Subsection (h)(9) Contribution in aid of construction (CIAC)
       AEP Texas requests that language be added to subsection (h)(9) that parallels the language

proposed for subsection (h)(8) to provide that before the interconnecting electric utility begins

construction of facilities to interconnect a large load customer, a large load customer must pay

CIAC unless the payment was executed in the initial construction services agreement. AEP Texas

acceptable form of payment for CIAC is cash. The resulting language in (h)(9)(D) would then be:

       The interconnecting electric utility may accept cash collateral as a form of payment for
       CIAC.

Commission of Texas (Commission) Staff’s questions regarding the discussion draft for large load
interconnection standards under PURA § 37.0561 and its comments on the discussion draft
language for 16 Tex. Admin. Code 25.194.

       is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request. The parameters should include
       a review of the details of the requests submitted to the applicable Distribution Service
       Provider (DSP) with legal authority to provide retail electric delivery service (applicable
       DSP) and whether any of the requests with the applicable DSP or in areas with other
       applicable DSPs would cause the customer to not pursue the request if the other is granted.
   •   The Commission does not need to list categories of information considered competitively
       sensitive information. The Commission should require all the reporting requirements in
       Senate Bill 6 to be provided by the customer to the interconnecting electric utility.
   •   AEP Texas supports a requirement that large-load customers notify the interconnecting
       electric utility and ERCOT about all changes to the information that was initially disclosed.
       AEP Texas also supports a requirement that large-load customers provide ongoing updates
       regarding the interconnecting facility throughout the life span of the interconnection of the
       facility.
   •   Senate Bill 6 sufficiently sets out the requirements for the security refund and there is no
       need for the Commission to expand or further outline those requirements.
   •   AEP Texas recommends that the Commission consider development of requirements that
       include a standard large-load customer interconnection study form and a standard

       for the way in which funds should be transferred among utilities for circumstances when

        AEP Texas requests that the proposed term "discretionary services agreement," be changed

The acronym "DSA" is already used for "delivery service agreements." AEP Texas also requests

that the Commission revise the definition to reflect that Senate Bill 6 provides options for types of

financial commitment other than securitization.

                    AEP TEXAS INC.'S COMMENTS ON DISCUSSION DRAFT

AEP Texas Inc. provides the following Executive Summary of its responses to the Public Utility
Commission of Texas (Commission) Staff's questions regarding the discussion draft for large load
interconnection standards under PURA § 37.0561 and its comments on the discussion draft
language for 16 Tex. Admin. Code 25.194.

    •   The Commission should define parameters for determining whether a large-load customer
        is pursuing a substantially similar interconnection request. The parameters should include
        a review of the details of the requests submitted to the applicable Distribution Service
        Provider (DSP) with legal authority to provide retail electric delivery service (applicable
        DSP) and whether any of the requests with the applicable DSP or in areas with other
        applicable DSPs would cause the customer to not pursue the request if the other is granted.
    •   The Commission does not need to list categories of information considered competitively
        sensitive information. The Commission should require all the reporting requirements in
        Senate Bill 6 to be provided by the customer to the interconnecting electric utility.
    •   AEP Texas supports a requirement that large-load customers notify the interconnecting
        electric utility and ERCOT about all changes to the information that was initially disclosed.
        AEP Texas also supports a requirement that large-load customers provide ongoing updates
        regarding the interconnecting facility throughout the life span of the interconnection of the
        facility.
    •   Senate Bill 6 sufficiently sets out the requirements for the security refund and there is no
        need for the Commission to expand or further outline those requirements.
    •   AEP Texas recommends that the Commission consider development of requirements that
        include a standard large-load customer interconnection study form and a standard
        construction service form. AEP Texas also requests that the Commission develop standards
        for the way in which funds should be transferred among utilities for circumstances when
        the applicable DSP facilitates the interconnection but is not necessarily the transmission
        service provider (TSP) for the specific point of interconnection.

        term "discretionary services agreement," be changed to "construction services agreement,"

        used for "delivery service agreements." AEP Texas also requests that the Commission

        commitment other than securitization.
